description:
FILED s470bj.  #1140's `escapes` fact records "the list of a foreach whose
variable is not PROVEN read-only" as an escape, and for a PLAIN (non-`my`) loop
variable -- the topic form `for (@a) {...}` and the statement modifier `EXPR for
@a` -- there is no proof available, because `$_` is a dynamically-scoped global
a callee can write.  So `for (@list) { print }` escapes `@list` today.

COST: only an optimization, and none was measured in the four populations at
filing (no `local-push` site and no `p-foreach-raw` loop was lost to it) --
because a topic loop never had `p-foreach-raw` in the first place (that arm
requires `:my`), and the loss only shows when the SAME array also carries a
push or a `my`-variable loop.

THE FIX IS THE SAME MECHANISM AS #1142: run the shared per-name gate list
`Pl::VarAnnotator::_text_gate_tags('$_', <body source>, 1)` over the loop BODY,
and treat a clean answer as a read.  The residue that must stay an escape: a
body containing any CALL (the callee can write `$_`, and in perl that write
reaches the element), and `$_` being localized/aliased further in.

Do #1142 first -- they share the oracle, and #1142 has a measured mover.
subject: A foreach/topic loop over @a whose loop variable is $_ escapes the array â prove $_ read-only from the body instead
